generativity.notes: The deep structure is the same in all five: one refusal shape, a record-driven registry, and a fix renderer over the agent's tokens. That part of the pattern is invariant. They split on the rest. A and C are domain-first: aliases just run, similarity comes from difflib, there are no named participants, and both check fixes before offering them (A by re-validating, C by replaying on a cloned store). B, D and E mirror the chapter's Structure table one module per participant (Suggester, Redirect table, Site tracker, Warning folder, Translator). They also copy the parts that don't fit a flat command language: the cross-kind step becomes 'use the other command', receiver lookup reads 'item' as a receiver, and site trackers hold the loop index. Within that group B is the most disciplined (one refusal builder), D adds canned fixes, and E adds four redirect tables and DEFAULTS. Every implementation except A drops the repeat prefix from fixes.

worse_is_better: A is the smallest (1355 source lines against 1613-2014) and gives the best repairs. Fixes are re-validated before they are offered (commands.py:350-365), keep the repeat prefix, and are withheld rather than invented (test_repair.py:59-66). A does without a SiteTracker class, a WarningFolder class (a closure, shop.py:52-67), a translator module, a Suggestion type, a redirect table and the cross-kind step. Two things that B, D and E carry are needed: a budgeted distance on the verb segment (A's difflib on whole names gives 'item.drop' the hint 'item.add'), and host_name as the exception class (A misreads it). The rest is not needed by this task: a named site tracker for a loop index, receiver lookup, E's four tables and DEFAULTS. The cross-kind option step does harm. C is equally lean in participants but packs the work into one 585-line class.
chapter_lessons: Missing force: a fix that runs is not a fix that is right. C, D and E make fixes pass 'run the fix and expect it to bind' by inventing values (C engine.py:574 qty=0 for 'abc'; D session.py:353 qty=2 for -1, language.py:133 'repeat 3: item.list'; E render.py:14-19 name=widget, and rm's fix turns 'remove all' into qty=1). Note 11 should add the negative law that only A states (test_repair.py:59-66): when the right value can't be derived, fix is None, and a fix must not change what the agent asked for.

The 'same name on another kind of value' step does not carry over to a flat command language. B, D and E read it as 'this option belongs to another command' and rewrite 'item.add ... cost=5' into 'report.margin ...' (B suggest.py:204-213, D suggester.py:226-233, E suggest.py:233-238), and all three lock that in tests. The chapter should say this step needs a real second kind of receiver, and should otherwise be dropped.

Fixes should rewrite only the failing part and keep its context. Four of five drop the 'repeat N:' prefix, so pasting the fix changes behaviour (B parse.py:377-394, C syntax.py:160-182, D session.py:97-110, E binder.py:249-269); only A keeps it (parser.py:47-49). Note 3 ('fixes are code, in the agent's names') should also say 'in the agent's line structure'.
Define host_name with an example and say it is None except under E_HOST. A read it as the canonical command name (diagnostics.py:63, shop.py:106) and tested it that way.

Some of the Structure table is goja-specific and gets copied as ornament: receiver lookup and the rows.count() translator (B translate.py:11-21, E translate.py:38-97) and a Site tracker class for what is just the loop index (B site.py, D session.py:32-44, E site.py:17-38). The chapter should mark the translator's receiver logic and the site tracker as needed only where agent code calls into host code or spans frames.

Apply the edit budget to the segment that differs, not to the whole namespaced name. difflib on 'item.drop' vs 'item.add' is inflated by the shared prefix and gives a confident wrong hint (A commands.py:417-420); B, D and E apply the budget to the verb and avoid it.

The chapter does not say whether a mined near-miss should refuse with a fix or just run. A and C made rm/ls legal aliases (no teaching), while B, D and E refuse. The 'errors against warnings' force suggests a third option worth naming: run the redirect and warn with the canonical name.

'One table, owned by the registry' got three readings: an attribute of the registry instance (B registry.py:109-112), a field of the suggester (D suggester.py:93-95), and module globals that leak across registries (E registry.py:137-196, test_ordering.py:41-45). The chapter should say the table is per registry and is checked against it (B suggest.py:129,194 is the right form).
